an appointment booked in for this morning with a practice nurse. I arrived 5 mins early, booked in on the machine. No problems, it said your wait is 5 mins, take a seat. Great. 25 minutes pass. I finally ask at the counter. Turns out the practice nurse was off sick. When I ring in sick for my job (that I have to take time out from to come to my medical appointments), I am meant to do it first thing and I'm sure most jobs are the same. So they must have known for at least an hour before this that she was sick and they would need to reschedule. They have me on their text service, could they not have texted me to let me know before I came out and wasted my time? And if that is somehow not possible, all the appointments in the check in machine are linked to the person who will be doing your appointment, so if someone is sick surely it should not be rocket science to have the machine flag up that you need to go to the counter when you try and check in?

It is especially annoying because I understand that the NHS wastes time and money when people miss their booked appointments, or are unable to attend and don't let anyone know. That's why I always attend my appointments, and if I could not I would ring up the relevant person as soon as I knew I couldn't go. However it does not go the other way! I had to take time out of work to come to this wasted appointment. They gave me a new appointment when I did go to the counter, so they get one extra star for that. However they have all this technology, automatic systems etc, why can none of it be used to help patients not come out to an appointment that isn't going to happen?

I felt so stupid because I had felt something might be wrong when the actual time for my appointment came and went, however I gave it more time before asking because I didn't want to be That person, who can't even wait 5 minutes, who is impatient and rude, so I sat around like a lemon...more fool me. My advise to you is don't worry about being that person. In fact, if you're seeing a practice nurse for a pre-booked appointment, I'd recommend asking straight away at the desk to check your nurse is actually there. It is the only way and I will definitely be doing this when I go to my rebooked appointment in a few days (time sensitive thing), in case she is still off
